_comment: Onboarding-focused set: how a student gets from zero to a real build/flash/debug loop on real hardware or the sim. Sources are this project's own MIT-licensed docs (cads-zero), not the copyrighted RM0090/PM0214 manuals - see README's licensing note. cads-zero's source repo is currently private, so this reads from the local checkout (localRoot) rather than fetching over HTTP; docBaseUrl (the public Pages site) is still used for citation URLs a student can actually click. Extending this to the full doc tree is mechanical.
_relevanceThresholdRationale: Calibrated against this pack's real score distribution (not copy-pasted from the Rust pack's 5.0 - see README). Unlike the Rust Book corpus, this one didn't cleanly separate: 'what does the RAM budget script check' (not actually covered by this pack) scored 7.51 by incidentally matching the literal token 'RAM' in an unrelated flash-bank/.ramfunc chunk, which sits ABOVE a genuinely good match ('what is the memory map', 5.92). No single scalar threshold separates both cleanly - 8.0 was chosen to eliminate the confirmed false positive, accepting the known, deliberate trade-off of also refusing one borderline-legitimate query ('what modules make up this project', 7.60) rather than risk more RAM-budget-style false groundings. A real BM25 limitation on heterogeneous (prose+tables+code) corpora, not something this threshold alone fully solves.
